feature.summary: Asks before the assistant uses a device capability. Explains microphone use on mobile and Chrome, asks before computer or browser control and before reading or writing a folder, shows each tool call for approval, and pairs a phone by code or QR. Scopes are wider than one call in several apps, and mobile pairing is switched off.

purpose.what_it_does: Gates device powers behind a question the person can answer, remembers the answer, and lets them revoke it. Also links another device to a desktop.
purpose.why_it_exists: The assistant can click, type, read files and run commands. People must stay in control of what it may touch, and a phone should only join a desktop the person owns.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using voice, computer use, browser control, folder tools, code agents or remote control.
use_cases: First voice dictation on Chrome shows a notice, then the browser asks
Desktop asks before the assistant controls the mouse and keyboard
Approve one shell command in the CLI
Show a pairing QR on desktop to link a phone

established.statement: Permission asks once, records the answer, does not re-prompt after refusal; a repeat request joins the open question.
Each tool approval covers one call.
Pairing is bound to the signed-in account and fails clearly on a wrong or expired code.
Browser control is granted per site origin and can be revoked.
Execution boundaries are explicit; nothing silently crosses Local, own key or Cloud.

acceptance_criteria: First computer-control request shows one dialog naming the action; a second request while it is open does not add a dialog
After Deny the same request in that session returns permission-denied without a new dialog
Removing a Chrome site's browser control stops runs on it
A folder not yet approved is not read by the assistant
Approve on one tool card runs that call only, if the policy is ask every time
A wrong or expired pairing code fails with a clear message
A phone on another account cannot claim a code
Mic refused on mobile shows how to turn it on

steps.what_happens: A command arrives at the desktop runtime and is mapped to a capability
If the state is 'prompt', a native dialog asks; the answer is recorded; Deny records a session denial
Granted: the command runs; single-use grants are consumed
Pairing: desktop calls /api/pair/initiate; the server mints a code bound to the account
Phone scans the code and calls /api/pair/claim; account mismatch returns 403
Desktop asks again to allow the phone itself before it connects

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: No model decides these permissions. The approvals gate what a model-driven agent may do on the device. Remote Control reads and steers coding sessions from the phone.

access_and_usage.account: Pairing needs a signed-in account on both devices. Other permissions work without an account for device-local actions [inferred].
access_and_usage.permissions: Per capability and scope on desktop (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/permissionManager.ts:334); per origin on Chrome; per workspace root for folders; per tool identity in VS Code (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/permissions/approvalScope.ts:60).
access_and_usage.subscription: Pairing is checked by a remote-control standing check on the server (apps/web/app/api/pair/initiate/route.ts:66). Which plans: unknown. Mobile reads a plan check for remote control (apps/mobile/app/(app)/companion/index.tsx:108).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Pairing requests rate limited under 'device-link' (apps/web/app/api/pair/initiate/route.ts:63); code lifetime 30 to 900 seconds, default 300 (route.ts:20, :25).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Desktop and CLI permissions are local and need no subscription. Pairing and Remote Control use the AGI relay, so they are cloud account features.

corrections.claim: Subscription: pairing is checked by a standing check on the server. Which plans: unknown.
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The plans are known. remoteControlStandingRefusal runs three checks in order: the workspace feature gate, the plan (403 plan_upgrade_required unless canUseBillingPlanCapability(plan,'remote_control')), then the screen-share kill switch. The capability maps to PAID_TIERS, so Free is refused. The desktop UI says 'Remote Control comes with paid plans.' The same check runs on claim. A plan lookup failure returns 503.
corrections.correction: Pairing needs a paid plan (every tier in PAID_TIERS), passing the workspace policy gate, and the screen-share switch being open. The same standing check runs on initiate and claim. Free is refused with 403 plan_upgrade_required.

corrections.claim: Desktop pairing needs the signed-in account and Remote Control switched on (initiate route :66)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The route requires a signed-in user, a rate limit, and the standing refusal check (workspace policy, paid plan, kill switch). 'Switched on' is not a user toggle at that line. The page leaves out the paid-plan requirement here and in the Local mode row.
corrections.correction: Needs a signed-in account on a paid plan, workspace policy allowing it, and the server-side screen-share switch open.

missing_facts: Remote Control pairing is gated by a paid plan, a workspace policy gate and a kill switch. Mobile also checks the plan client-side via canUseBillingPlanCapability(tier,'remote_control'). Free users get 403 plan_upgrade_required. The page says the plans are unknown. See apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts:62-125 and packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:352.

The page leaves out that computer.use, host.remote, shell.execute, application.control, browser.cdp and git.destructive are all high-risk (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/capabilities.ts:67-74). So computer-control prompts never offer 'Always allow' and last only until the app quits. This resolves the page's own Unknown item about computer.use.

The CLI refuses a shell tool in an untrusted workspace unless the user approves that one command, and no auto-approval mode waives it. Workspace-layer 'Allow' policies are downgraded to 'Ask' until the repo is trusted (apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/mod.rs:1784-1815). The page only mentions 'untrusted shell refusal' in passing.
